tasks.name: Create a unique controller report directory
tasks.description: Creates a new temporary directory on the control node or AAP execution environment for this run’s reports. Each run has its own output location.

tasks.name: Seed AAP job artifacts before any target connection
tasks.description: When job-artifact publishing is enabled, records an incomplete assessment before connecting to targets. This initial artifact is unknown, so an interrupted run cannot appear cleared.

tasks.name: Load the bundled NCSC snapshot without network requests
tasks.description: Reads data/ncsc/snapshot.json from the project checkout. Discovery uses this pinned copy and does not download current NCSC data.

tasks.name: Validate the bundled snapshot
tasks.description: Checks the snapshot commit format, nonempty pages, page content and successful stored HTTP statuses. Invalid input stops the play and directs the operator to the separate refresh playbook.

tasks.name: Store the source snapshot privately
tasks.description: Saves the exact NCSC input as ncsc.json with owner-only file permissions, preserving the source used for this run.

tasks.name: Seed every scoped host as unknown before connections
tasks.description: Writes an unknown placeholder for every host in php_targets before connections begin. A host without a completed assessment retains an explicit unassessed record.

tasks.name: Collect package, process, runtime, and container evidence
tasks.description: For targets whose configured shell is not PowerShell, includes the Linux collector below. Passes inventory-defined phpdetect_runtimes as the list of mapped runtimes; collected details are suppressed in normal task logs.

tasks.name: Collect native Windows PHP evidence
tasks.description: For targets configured with a PowerShell shell, includes the Windows collector instead. Branch selection is based on inventory shell configuration, not an automatic Windows connection probe.

tasks.name: Build product candidate matches without treating matches as clearance
tasks.description: For each inventory-supplied phpdetect_products entry, searches NCSC snapshot lines for its escaped ncsc_term. Matches remain unknown and do not prove product installation or patch status.

tasks.name: Save the host assessment on the controller
tasks.description: Combines the assessment with inventory host name, connection address and product matches. Writes it back to the control node with owner-only permissions, replacing that host’s placeholder.

tasks.name: Assemble all host results including unreachable seeds
tasks.description: Reads the saved result for every scoped host, including any unknown placeholders left by failed or unreachable collection. Final assembly must itself run for a consolidated report to be produced.

tasks.name: Write the consolidated assessment
tasks.description: Writes summary.json with host assessments, NCSC revision/date and counts of affected and unknown hosts. Affected runtime evidence can flag a host; a patched subset does not clear a host.

tasks.name: Preserve discovery evidence in AAP job artifacts
tasks.description: When enabled, publishes the assembled hosts and NCSC commit using set_stats so AAP retains them after the execution environment exits. Complete means report assembly completed, not that every host was fully inspected.

tasks.name: Show private output directory
tasks.description: Prints the private report directory and reminds the operator that unknown findings need follow-up. A separate deployment process publishes a chosen report to the dashboard; discovery does not update the public page automatically.

tasks.name: Initialize conservative collection state
tasks.description: Initializes empty collections and conservative defaults before gathering evidence. No runtime starts with an assumed patched status.

tasks.name: Read operating system without changing the host
tasks.description: Runs uname -s to identify the target kernel family without collecting broad Ansible facts.

tasks.name: Collect Linux evidence
tasks.description: Runs the following block only when uname reports Linux. Other non-Windows platforms do not receive Linux package or process assessment.

tasks.name: Read distribution release
tasks.description: Reads /etc/os-release as data to identify the distribution and release.

tasks.name: Parse distribution release
tasks.description: Parses uppercase release keys into a dictionary used when comparing vendor evidence with the host platform.

tasks.name: Read installed Debian package revisions
tasks.description: Queries dpkg for installed package names, full revisions and installation state. Keeps the complete database for exact ownership and package comparisons.

tasks.name: Read installed RPM package revisions when Debian tools are absent
tasks.description: If the Debian query failed, queries RPM for package name and epoch:version-release.architecture. Vendor release suffixes are retained.

tasks.name: Determine package manager evidence
tasks.description: Sets the detected package-manager family from successful query results; unavailable package evidence remains unknown.

tasks.name: Parse the installed package database
tasks.description: Includes the package parsing tasks below to convert query output into a name-to-exact-version dictionary.

tasks.name: Find common PHP installations without executing them
tasks.description: Searches common executable, selected hosting-panel and Apache-module directories for PHP-named ELF files. Reads file signatures rather than executing candidates.

tasks.name: Retain unmapped installation candidates
tasks.description: Deduplicates and retains candidate paths. These candidates are not automatically promoted to mapped or verified serving runtimes.

tasks.name: Read process names without command arguments
tasks.description: Reads process IDs and command names with ps, without collecting process command-line arguments in the report.

tasks.name: Identify PHP executables under a different process root
tasks.description: Compares process roots to the host root for PHP/FrankenPHP executable paths. A different root is a lead for a container or chroot; inaccessible processes may be skipped by this scan.

tasks.name: Keep foreign-root candidates explicitly unknown
tasks.description: Saves foreign-root PID/path findings as unknown and explicitly asks for separate container or chroot assessment.

tasks.name: Inspect Nginx configuration privately
tasks.description: Runs nginx -T with task output hidden from normal logs to read effective routing configuration.

tasks.name: Retain only Nginx routing directives without credential URLs
tasks.description: Keeps only server_name, fastcgi_pass and proxy_pass hints, excluding lines containing @ to avoid credential-bearing URLs.

tasks.name: Read Apache virtual-host mappings privately
tasks.description: Tries Apache control binaries with -S to collect virtual-host information, with raw task output hidden.

tasks.name: Retain successful Apache routing hints
tasks.description: Adds only successful Apache output to the routing hints. These hints are not a verified end-to-end website-to-PHP mapping.

tasks.name: Assess each explicitly mapped runtime
tasks.description: For each explicitly configured runtime, includes the ownership, live-file and classification tasks below. Unmapped candidates do not receive this assessment.

tasks.name: Enumerate Docker containers
tasks.description: Lists all Docker container IDs, including stopped containers. Missing Docker access leaves container coverage unknown.

tasks.name: Inspect container identity without logging full configuration
tasks.description: Inspects each container with full task output hidden so sensitive configuration is not printed in the job log.

tasks.name: Keep only container identity and running state
tasks.description: Retains only container ID/name, image ID/reference and running state. Every container starts and remains unknown in this collector.

tasks.name: Read container CLI PHP version as supporting evidence only
tasks.description: Only when the optional probe is enabled and a container is running, executes php -n -v inside it. This is CLI evidence, not verification of the serving process.

tasks.name: Record incomplete Linux discovery coverage
tasks.description: Records missing package access, unavailable Docker, failed container inspections and mapped-runtime process visibility gaps.

tasks.name: Retain version-only evidence linked to each running container
tasks.description: Associates successful PHP CLI version lines with their container IDs. A CLI version never changes the container’s unknown patch status.

tasks.name: Assemble the host report without inferring complete coverage
tasks.description: Builds the host report with package, runtime, candidate, routing, process and container evidence. Host status is affected if a mapped runtime is affected; otherwise it remains unknown. Unsupported platforms get an explicit coverage gap.

tasks.name: Parse installed Debian package records in one operation
tasks.description: For Debian systems, filters package records to installed entries and creates a dictionary of package names and exact versions.

tasks.name: Parse installed RPM package records
tasks.description: For RPM systems, turns query records into the same package dictionary format, preserving epoch, release and architecture.

tasks.name: Initialize runtime evidence
tasks.description: Loads the mapped runtime’s supplied vendor evidence and resets package-owner, process and visibility-gap state for that runtime.

tasks.name: Resolve the mapped artifact
tasks.description: Resolves the configured artifact path with readlink -f so ownership and process checks refer to its canonical path.

tasks.name: Read the Debian owner of the mapped artifact
tasks.description: On Debian systems, asks dpkg-query which package owns the resolved artifact.

tasks.name: Read the RPM owner of the mapped artifact
tasks.description: On RPM systems, asks rpm which package owns the resolved artifact.

tasks.name: Record the owning package
tasks.description: Stores a successfully determined owner. Missing ownership evidence prevents vendor build confirmation.

tasks.name: Compare every vendor-approved package revision
tasks.description: Compares every package revision listed in the supplied evidence with the exact installed revision. An empty or mismatched evidence set cannot establish a vendor-confirmed result.

tasks.name: Inspect all live instances and their file mappings without changing them
tasks.description: As root, scans host-root processes for the mapped executable or module. Compares executable and loaded-file device/inode identities against disk, detects stale/deleted files and records visibility failures. PID|true is current file identity, not proof of a patch.

tasks.name: Parse process evidence
tasks.description: Converts PID|true/false output into structured process records for the classifier.

tasks.name: Record process visibility gaps with their cause
tasks.description: Preserves each gap|PID|cause line so a failure to inspect processes is explained rather than treated as a clean result.

tasks.name: Report a failed inspection that produced no gap lines (for example bash missing)
tasks.description: If the inspection command failed without structured gap lines, records its exit status and error text as a visibility gap.

tasks.name: Evaluate vendor and running-build evidence
tasks.description: Includes the classification tasks below with exact package matching, ownership, OS facts, process evidence and inspection visibility.

tasks.name: Append runtime assessment
tasks.description: Adds the runtime result, reason, sites supplied in inventory, process details and vendor evidence. Internal exposure is P2; internet or unknown exposure is P1. Exposure is inventory-supplied, not externally tested.

tasks.name: Check complete vendor evidence for the exact operating system and package owner
tasks.description: Checks supplied advisory URL/date/channel/CVE fields, exact OS/release, nonempty package revisions and artifact ownership. Separately requires at least one live instance with all current file identities and complete visibility for running-build verification. It does not fetch or authenticate the advisory.

tasks.name: Keep incomplete results unknown
tasks.description: Sets affected only for matching affected vendor evidence. Sets patched only for matching patched vendor evidence plus verified live files. All other combinations remain unknown.

tasks.name: Explain every reason a runtime is not cleared
tasks.description: Explains incomplete vendor evidence, visibility gaps, absent live instances, stale processes or unsupported vendor status. This reason travels with the runtime record.

tasks.name: Collect native Windows PHP file, process, and IIS evidence without executing candidate binaries
tasks.description: Runs one inline PowerShell collector: reads php.exe/php-cgi.exe process paths; searches common PHP directories to depth two; reads executable versions and SHA-256 hashes; gathers IIS website names, paths and bindings; and records OS information and gaps. Candidate binaries are not executed. All Windows patch statuses remain unknown because vendor, serving-site and loaded-build verification are not implemented.

tasks.name: Preserve the Windows assessment in the common report schema
tasks.description: Parses the PowerShell JSON into the common assessment schema so Windows hosts can be reported alongside Linux and container evidence.
